title: Cull, edit, and sequence a shoot
description: Collapse near-identical takes, score what survives, cut to length, then build the opening, body, and close in order and critique the sequence as a whole.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: wf-photo-03
  title: Cull, edit, and sequence a shoot
  description: Collapse near-identical takes, score what survives, cut to length, then build the opening,
    body, and close in order and critique the sequence as a whole.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: Turn a full take from a shoot into an edit that reads as one body of work, where every surviving
    frame has a stated job in the sequence and the cut is defensible.
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 4
    onFailure: preserve-completed
    requireApprovalFor:
      - n-approval
  nodes:
    - id: n-intake
      kind: input
      name: The full take and the story it is for
      summary: The full take and the story it is for
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - assets
          - instructions
        properties:
          assets:
            type: array
            minItems: 1
            maxItems: 12
            items:
              type: object
              required:
                - uri
                - mediaType
              properties:
                uri:
                  type: string
                  description: A host-provided data URL, local file reference, uploaded-asset identifier,
                    or authorized HTTPS URL. Ladder Graph does not upload or fetch the asset.
                mediaType:
                  type: string
                  pattern: ^(image|audio|video|application)/
                name:
                  type: string
          instructions:
            type: string
          sourceRights:
            type: string
            description: User-supplied rights, consent, release, or provenance context when relevant.
          workflowFields:
            type: object
            required:
              - stated_story
              - genre
              - target_count
              - viewing_context
            properties:
              stated_story: {}
              genre: {}
              target_count: {}
              viewing_context: {}
        x-ladder-input-mode: mixed
    - id: n-dedupe
      kind: transform
      name: Collapse the bursts to one frame each
      summary: collapse near-identical frames from the same burst or setup to the strongest representative
        of each
      config:
        operation: deduplicate
        expression: collapse near-identical frames from the same burst or setup to the strongest representative
          of each
    - id: n-score
      kind: agent
      templateRef: photo-02
      name: Score every surviving frame
      summary: Score every surviving frame on its own terms before anything is cut.
      role: Analyst working frame geometry, subject placement, edges, and visual weight.
      prompt: You are a Composition & Framing Analyst. You work the geometry of the frame — where the
        subject sits, what the edges do, how negative space and visual weight balance, where the eye enters
        and where it leaves — and you say what the composition is doing for the picture rather than scoring
        it against a rule. You treat compositional 'rules' as descriptions of what often works and not
        as requirements, you flag the edge and background problems photographers stop seeing in their
        own work, and you separate a frame that breaks a convention deliberately from one that breaks
        it accidentally.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - decision-analysis
          - evaluation
          - domain-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - frame
          - strength
          - role_in_set
          - reason
        properties:
          frame: {}
          strength: {}
          role_in_set: {}
          reason: {}
    - id: n-rank
      kind: transform
      name: Rank by strength
      summary: sort by strength against the stated story descending, then by what the frame contributes
        that no other frame does
      config:
        operation: sort
        expression: sort by strength against the stated story descending, then by what the frame contributes
          that no other frame does
    - id: n-cut
      kind: transform
      name: Cut to the target length
      summary: take the first target_count frames as the working edit
      config:
        operation: slice
        expression: take the first target_count frames as the working edit
    - id: n-section1
      kind: agent
      templateRef: photo-07
      name: Opening frames
      summary: The frames that set the terms of the sequence.
      role: Picture editor selecting and ordering a set so it reads as one body of work.
      prompt: You are a Photo Editor & Sequencing Specialist. You select against the story rather than
        against individual frame quality — the strongest single picture is often the wrong opener — and
        you order a set so that adjacent frames do work for each other rather than repeating each other.
        You cut redundancy hard, including frames the photographer is attached to, and you say what each
        surviving frame is doing in the sequence, because an edit nobody can explain is a gallery, not
        a story.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - writing-editing
          - domain-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-section2
      kind: agent
      templateRef: photo-07
      name: Body of the sequence
      summary: The frames that carry the story and its variation.
      role: Picture editor selecting and ordering a set so it reads as one body of work.
      prompt: You are a Photo Editor & Sequencing Specialist. You select against the story rather than
        against individual frame quality — the strongest single picture is often the wrong opener — and
        you order a set so that adjacent frames do work for each other rather than repeating each other.
        You cut redundancy hard, including frames the photographer is attached to, and you say what each
        surviving frame is doing in the sequence, because an edit nobody can explain is a gallery, not
        a story.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - writing-editing
          - domain-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-section3
      kind: agent
      templateRef: photo-07
      name: Closing frames
      summary: The frames that land the sequence.
      role: Picture editor selecting and ordering a set so it reads as one body of work.
      prompt: You are a Photo Editor & Sequencing Specialist. You select against the story rather than
        against individual frame quality — the strongest single picture is often the wrong opener — and
        you order a set so that adjacent frames do work for each other rather than repeating each other.
        You cut redundancy hard, including frames the photographer is attached to, and you say what each
        surviving frame is doing in the sequence, because an edit nobody can explain is a gallery, not
        a story.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - writing-editing
          - domain-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-assemble
      kind: aggregator
      name: Assemble the edit in viewing order
      summary: Preserve the declared order exactly; a sequence is ordered assembly, not a merge of opinions.
      config:
        aggregation: concat
    - id: n-critique
      kind: teacher
      inlineRole: true
      name: Critique the sequence as a whole
      summary: Critique feedback from a host-resolved teacher model.
      role: Host-resolved teacher model
      prompt: 'You are the critique teacher for this edit. Read it in order, the way a viewer will: where
        does the sequence repeat itself, where does a strong single frame stop the flow, where does the
        edit lose the story, and is the opener doing the job an opener has to do? Comment on the sequence,
        not on individual frames in isolation.'
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
      config:
        teacherModel: host:teacher-model
        feedbackMode: critique
    - id: n-quality
      kind: evaluate
      inlineRole: true
      name: Score the edit
      summary: Evaluate narrative arc, absence of redundancy, and whether each frame has a stated job.
      role: Deterministic metric evaluator
      prompt: Evaluate the upstream result against narrative arc, absence of redundancy, and whether each
        frame has a stated job. Return a score, pass/fail verdict, the evidence behind the verdict, remaining
        uncertainty, and the smallest corrective action. Do not claim programmatic measurement unless
        the host supplies the required tool.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - score
          - passed
          - reasons
        properties:
          score:
            type: number
          passed:
            type: boolean
          reasons:
            type: array
            items:
              type: string
      config:
        threshold: 0.8
    - id: n-accept
      kind: condition
      name: Edit holds?
      summary: Route on quality.passed.
      config:
        expression: quality.passed
        branches:
          - label: Accept
            when: 'true'
          - label: Re-edit
            when: 'false'
    - id: n-revise
      kind: agent
      templateRef: photo-07
      name: Re-cut against the sequence critique
      summary: Re-cut against the sequence critique.
      role: Picture editor selecting and ordering a set so it reads as one body of work.
      prompt: You are a Photo Editor & Sequencing Specialist. You select against the story rather than
        against individual frame quality — the strongest single picture is often the wrong opener — and
        you order a set so that adjacent frames do work for each other rather than repeating each other.
        You cut redundancy hard, including frames the photographer is attached to, and you say what each
        surviving frame is doing in the sequence, because an edit nobody can explain is a gallery, not
        a story.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - writing-editing
          - domain-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-approval
      kind: approval
      name: Photographer signs off on the final edit
      summary: Pause for the photographer; on timeout, escalate.
    - id: workflow-output
      kind: output
      name: Released deliverable
      summary: Return the completed Cull, edit, and sequence a shoot deliverable, the evidence behind
        it, and every unresolved item.
  edges:
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-1
      from: n-intake
      to: n-dedupe
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-2
      from: n-dedupe
      to: n-score
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-3
      from: n-score
      to: n-rank
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-4
      from: n-rank
      to: n-cut
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-5
      from: n-cut
      to: n-section1
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-6
      from: n-cut
      to: n-section2
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-7
      from: n-cut
      to: n-section3
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-8
      from: n-section1
      to: n-assemble
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-9
      from: n-section2
      to: n-assemble
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-10
      from: n-section3
      to: n-assemble
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-11
      from: n-assemble
      to: n-critique
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-12
      from: n-critique
      to: n-quality
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-13
      from: n-quality
      to: n-accept
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-14
      from: n-accept
      to: n-approval
      kind: control
      condition: 'true'
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-15
      from: n-accept
      to: n-revise
      kind: control
      condition: 'false'
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-16
      from: n-revise
      to: n-approval
      kind: data
    - id: wf-photo-03-edge-17
      from: n-approval
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
      condition: approved
